title: Export button stays disabled after choosing a date range
author: Priya Shah
body: The export button stays disabled after I choose a valid date range. Refreshing the page fixes it temporarily.

comments.author: Priya Shah
comments.text: I can reproduce this in Chrome 129 on macOS. The date picker shows the correct range, but the action never enables.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: Thanks for the clear steps. We found a stale state update and are preparing a fix.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: That matches what I am seeing. I can test a preview build if that helps.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: A preview would be useful. Could you also try a range that crosses into a new month?

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: I tried July 29 through August 3. The dates remain selected, but Export is still disabled.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: That confirms the timezone normalization bug. We are checking the end-of-day conversion now.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: The same steps fail in Safari 18, so this does not look Chrome-specific.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: The fix is in our beta build. We now compare calendar dates before converting the range to UTC; please let us know if your test passes.

comments.author: Jordan Lee
comments.text: Same issue here. The selected range is visible in the toolbar, but the export control stays disabled. Screenshot attached.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: I can see the mismatch in the screenshot. Does clearing the range and selecting it again enable the button?

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We have a fix in review. It addresses a stale selection flag that was not refreshed after both dates were chosen.

replies.author: Jordan Lee
replies.text: Clearing and reselecting did not help on my account. Happy to retest when the fix ships.

comments.author: Elena Garcia
comments.text: Selecting the start date first and the end date second still leaves Export disabled until I refresh the report.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We have isolated this to the range-change handler. The date inputs update correctly, but the export eligibility state can lag behind.

comments.author: Noah Williams
comments.text: For comparison, exporting with the preset 'Last 30 days' works. Only manually selected ranges reproduce it for me.

comments.author: Ava Patel
comments.text: I see it on Windows 11 in Edge 128. Changing the end date twice sometimes enables the button, but the resulting CSV is empty.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Thanks, Ava. An empty export would be a separate symptom of the same stale range value. We are adding that case to our regression checks.

comments.author: Samir Khan
comments.text: My account is set to Europe/London. A range within one day works, while a range spanning the daylight-saving transition stays disabled.

comments.author: Priya Shah
comments.text: I tested the workaround of opening the report in a new tab. The chosen dates survive, but the export action remains disabled.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We can reproduce the daylight-saving case. The comparison currently uses timestamps instead of the dates shown in the picker.

comments.author: Liam O'Connor
comments.text: The keyboard flow has the same problem: after tabbing out of the end-date field, the selected range is valid but Export is unavailable.

comments.author: Zoe Martin
comments.text: I can make the button appear by switching to another report and back. It is a useful temporary workaround, though the first export attempt still fails.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The report switch forces a full refresh of the selection state, which explains why that workaround helps. We are avoiding that extra reload in the fix.

comments.author: Ethan Brooks
comments.text: This also happens with the custom date range in the activity export, not only the revenue report.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Good catch. Both export screens share the date-range control, so we will verify the patch in each one.

comments.author: Isabella Chen
comments.text: If I choose the same day for both ends, Export enables. As soon as I extend the range by one day, it turns disabled again.

comments.author: Oliver Smith
comments.text: The bug started after the September interface update. I did not see it in the previous version.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: That lines up with the date-picker refactor in the September release. We have narrowed the regression to the new controlled input path.

comments.author: Grace Kim
comments.text: A hard refresh fixes the button for one session, but navigating away and returning causes the issue again.

comments.author: Daniel Foster
comments.text: I use a UTC+10 workspace. A range ending today appears to be treated as tomorrow when the server validates it.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We found an off-by-one conversion near midnight UTC. The fix will preserve the selected local calendar days end to end.

comments.author: Mia Thompson
comments.text: The CSV export works if I use the quick range buttons, so this appears limited to the two manual date fields.

comments.author: Lucas Brown
comments.text: I see the disabled state on Firefox 130 as well. It persists after signing out and back in.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We have confirmed Firefox is affected too. This is application state, not a browser cache issue.

comments.author: Amara Johnson
comments.text: Our finance team cannot export a quarter-to-date report. Preset ranges remain usable, but we need a specific cutoff date.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We understand the impact for scheduled reporting. I will post here as soon as the patch is available to verify.

comments.author: Henry Wilson
comments.text: When I paste dates into both fields, the range looks valid but Export stays inactive. Selecting the dates from the calendar has the same result.

comments.author: Nina Park
comments.text: The issue occurs in an incognito window too, with extensions disabled and a fresh login.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: That rules out extension interference. We appreciate the clean reproduction steps.

comments.author: Theo Wilson
comments.text: The date labels are correct after switching the workspace timezone, but the export state does not recalculate until I reload.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Workspace timezone changes were missing a recalculation hook. We are including timezone changes in the same state refresh.

comments.author: Sofia Alvarez
comments.text: I can reproduce with a one-week range and with a full year. Range length does not seem to matter.

comments.author: Benjamin Scott
comments.text: For accessibility testing, the disabled state is announced correctly, but it never updates after both dates are entered.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Thanks for checking the screen reader behavior. The updated state notification is part of our keyboard and accessibility test plan.

comments.author: Layla Hassan
comments.text: On an iPad, the calendar closes after I select the end date, but the export action stays gray until I rotate the screen.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The rotation forces a layout update and masks the stale state. We will add the tablet flow to the verification matrix.

comments.author: Jack Turner
comments.text: I recorded the network panel: there is no export request while the button is disabled, even though the request preview contains both dates.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: That is expected while the control is disabled. The request preview confirms the selected dates reach the client correctly.

comments.author: Ruby Evans
comments.text: The affected report has a saved filter. Removing the filter did not change the disabled state.

comments.author: Omar Ali
comments.text: I can export after clearing the dates and choosing a preset, then go back and manually select the dates. It takes a few tries.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: That sequence refreshes the derived range value. We are using your steps as an additional regression case.

comments.author: Chloe Davis
comments.text: My teammate and I both see it, but another teammate on the older dashboard layout can export normally.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The older layout uses the previous date selector. This confirms the regression is isolated to the new dashboard experience.

comments.author: Mateo Ruiz
comments.text: This morning I can reproduce it on the staging workspace using the same account and browser as production.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The patch has passed our unit checks and is now in staging. We are validating CSV, XLSX, and scheduled exports.

comments.author: Priya Shah
comments.text: I tested the staging build with the August 1–31 range. Export enabled immediately and the downloaded CSV contained the expected rows.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: Excellent, thank you for checking both the button state and the exported rows. We are finishing the timezone test cases.

comments.author: Ava Patel
comments.text: I retested in Edge on Windows with a range crossing the month boundary. The button enables correctly in staging.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The fix is queued for the next release after our final checks. We will keep this issue open until production is updated.

comments.author: Samir Khan
comments.text: I verified the daylight-saving range in the staging workspace set to Europe/London. It now enables without a refresh.

comments.author: Elena Garcia
comments.text: The manual range also works with the browser zoom set to 125%, which used to require clicking away from the picker.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: We included zoom and narrow viewport checks to ensure the action state does not depend on a layout event.

comments.author: Noah Williams
comments.text: I tested custom ranges in both the activity and revenue reports. Both export buttons are enabled now.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The production release is rolling out to a small group now. We will expand it after monitoring export errors.

comments.author: Daniel Foster
comments.text: The UTC+10 workspace now treats today's end date as today. My morning report includes the correct final day.

comments.author: Grace Kim
comments.text: After the rollout, I selected a custom range, navigated to another report, and returned. The selection remained usable.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.text: The rollout is complete. Please reply if you still see a disabled action after choosing both dates.

comments.author: Jordan Lee
comments.text: Confirmed fixed on my account. The CSV download starts as soon as I select the end date.

comments.author: Priya Shah
comments.text: Production works for me now in Chrome and Safari, including ranges that cross a month and timezone boundary. Thanks for following through.
